targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  AVG(score) :: numeric(4, 2) AS "Avg Rating",
  COUNT(*) AS "Rating Count",
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS "Raters"
FROM
  comment_scores
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project);

SELECT
  score::text AS "Score",
  COUNT(*)    AS "Ratings"
FROM comment_scores
WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at::timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY score
ORDER BY score;

SELECT
  $__timeGroup(received_at :: timestamptz, '1w') AS time,
  AVG(score) :: numeric(4, 2) AS "Avg Rating",
  COUNT(*) AS "Ratings"
FROM
  comment_scores
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY
  1;

SELECT
  date_trunc('day', received_at::timestamptz) AS "time",
  AVG(score)::numeric(4,2) AS "Avg Rating"
FROM comment_scores
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(received_at::timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT
  $__timeGroup(rc.received_at::timestamptz, '1w') AS time,
  -- COUNT(*)                                        AS "Comments Posted",
  -- COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id)                      AS "Comments Rated",
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) / COUNT(*), 1) AS "Coverage"
FROM review_comments rc
LEFT JOIN comment_scores cs ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(rc.received_at::timestamptz)
  AND rc.project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT
  project_path AS "Project",
  COUNT(*) AS "Ratings"
FROM
  comment_scores
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY
  project_path
ORDER BY
  "Ratings" DESC;

SELECT
  INITCAP(rc.severity) AS "Severity",
  COUNT(cs.id) AS "Ratings",
  AVG(cs.score) :: numeric(4, 2) AS "Avg Rating"
FROM
  comment_scores cs
  JOIN review_comments rc ON rc.note_id = cs.note_id
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(cs.received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND cs.project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY
  rc.severity
ORDER BY
  "Avg Rating" DESC;

SELECT
  COALESCE(rc.model, '(pre-0009, unknown)')   AS "Model",
  COUNT(cs.id)                                AS "Ratings",
  AVG(cs.score)::numeric(4,2)                 AS "Avg Rating",
  COUNT(DISTINCT rc.id)                       AS "Comments"
FROM review_comments rc
LEFT JOIN comment_scores cs
       ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
      AND $__timeFilter(cs.received_at::timestamptz)
WHERE rc.project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY "Ratings" DESC;

panels.title: Findings rating by model (actual model per comment)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  r.reviewer_version AS "Version",
  ROUND(AVG(s.score) :: numeric, 2) AS "Average Rating",
  COUNT(*) AS "Ratings",
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.note_id) AS "Comments Rated",
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS "Comments Posted"
FROM
  review_comments c
  JOIN review_runs r ON r.id = c.review_run_id
  LEFT JOIN comment_scores s ON s.note_id = c.note_id
WHERE
  r.project_path IN ($project)
  AND $__timeFilter(r.timestamp :: timestamptz)
GROUP BY
  r.reviewer_version
HAVING
  COUNT(s.id) > 0
ORDER BY
  lpad(
    coalesce(
      substring(
        r.reviewer_version
        from
          '^v?(\d+)'
      ),
      '0'
    ),
    5,
    '0'
  ) || lpad(
    coalesce(
      substring(
        r.reviewer_version
        from
          '^v?\d+\.(\d+)'
      ),
      '0'
    ),
    5,
    '0'
  ) || lpad(
    coalesce(
      substring(
        r.reviewer_version
        from
          '^v?\d+\.\d+\.(\d+)'
      ),
      '0'
    ),
    5,
    '0'
  ) DESC;

-- One row per (note, rater): comment_scores is unique on
-- (note_id, user_id, emoji), so a rater who clicked 3, reconsidered, clicked 4
-- and never revoked the 3 leaves two rows — COUNT(*) scored them twice and
-- AVG(score) blended a rating they had abandoned. Latest click wins.
WITH canonical AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (note_id, user_id)
    note_id, user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
  FROM comment_scores
  WHERE $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
    AND project_path IN ($project)
  ORDER BY note_id, user_id, received_at DESC, emoji DESC
)
SELECT
  user_name AS "Rater",
  username AS "Username",
  COUNT(*) AS "Ratings Given",
  AVG(score) :: numeric(4, 2) AS "Avg Given"
FROM canonical
GROUP BY user_name, username
ORDER BY "Ratings Given" DESC;

panels.title: Rater leaderboard
panels.description: Deduped to one rating per (comment, rater) — see the query.

targets.rawSql:
WITH per_user AS (
  SELECT
    note_id,
    user_id,
    AVG(score) AS user_score
  FROM
    comment_scores
  WHERE
    $__timeFilter(received_at :: timestamptz)
    AND project_path IN ($project)
  GROUP BY
    note_id,
    user_id
)
SELECT
  rc.project_path AS "Project",
  'https://gitlab.example.com/' || rc.project_path || '/-/merge_requests/' || rc.mr_id || '#note_' || rc.note_id AS "Link",
  -- rc.mr_id AS "MR",
  rc.file AS "File",
  rc.line AS "Line",
  INITCAP(rc.severity) AS "Severity",
  COUNT(*) AS "Raters",
  AVG(pu.user_score) :: numeric(4, 2) AS "Avg Rating"
FROM
  per_user pu
  JOIN review_comments rc ON rc.note_id = pu.note_id
GROUP BY
  rc.note_id,
  rc.project_path,
  rc.mr_id,
  rc.file,
  rc.line,
  rc.severity
ORDER BY
  "Avg Rating" ASC,
  "Raters" DESC
LIMIT
  20;

SELECT
  -- cs.project_path AS "Project",
  'https://gitlab.example.com/' || cs.project_path || '/-/merge_requests/' || cs.mr_id || '#note_' || cs.note_id AS "Link",
  cs.score AS "Score",
  rr.reviewer_version AS "Version",
  cs.user_name AS "User"
FROM
  comment_scores cs
  INNER JOIN review_comments rc ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
  INNER JOIN review_runs rr ON rr.id = rc.review_run_id
WHERE
  $__timeFilter(cs.awarded_at::timestamptz)
  AND cs.project_path IN ($project)
ORDER BY
  cs.awarded_at DESC

WITH replies AS (
  SELECT cr.parent_note_id, cr.parent_kind, cr.author_username, cr.body,
         COALESCE(NULLIF(cr.noted_at,'')::timestamptz, cr.received_at::timestamptz) AS reply_time
  FROM comment_replies cr
)
SELECT
  'https://gitlab.example.com/' || COALESCE(rc.project_path, rs.project_path)
    || '/-/merge_requests/' || COALESCE(rc.mr_id, rs.mr_id)
    || '#note_' || r.parent_note_id                    AS "Link",
  INITCAP(COALESCE(r.parent_kind, 'finding'))          AS "Kind",
  r.body                                               AS "Reply",
  r.author_username                                    AS "Replied by"
FROM replies r
LEFT JOIN review_comments  rc ON rc.note_id = r.parent_note_id
LEFT JOIN review_summaries rs ON rs.note_id = r.parent_note_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(r.reply_time)
  AND COALESCE(rc.project_path, rs.project_path) IN ($project)
ORDER BY r.reply_time DESC;

SELECT
  AVG(ss.score)::numeric(4,2)   AS "Avg Summary Rating",
  COUNT(ss.id)                  AS "Ratings",
  COUNT(DISTINCT rs.note_id)    AS "Summaries Posted"
FROM review_summaries rs
LEFT JOIN summary_scores ss
       ON ss.note_id = rs.note_id
      AND $__timeFilter(ss.received_at::timestamptz)
WHERE rs.project_path IN ($project);

SELECT
  'https://gitlab.example.com/' || rs.project_path
    || '/-/merge_requests/' || rs.mr_id || '#note_' || rs.note_id  AS "Link",
  COALESCE(rs.model, '(unknown)')   AS "Model",
  AVG(ss.score)::numeric(4,2)       AS "Avg Rating",
  COUNT(DISTINCT ss.id)             AS "Ratings",
  COUNT(DISTINCT cr.note_id)        AS "Replies",
  rs.mr_author_username             AS "MR Author"
FROM review_summaries rs
LEFT JOIN summary_scores ss ON ss.note_id = rs.note_id
LEFT JOIN comment_replies cr
       ON cr.parent_note_id = rs.note_id AND cr.parent_kind = 'summary'
WHERE rs.project_path IN ($project)
  AND $__timeFilter(rs.received_at::timestamptz)
GROUP BY rs.note_id, rs.project_path, rs.mr_id, rs.model, rs.mr_author_username
ORDER BY "Avg Rating" ASC NULLS LAST, "Ratings" DESC
LIMIT 50;

panels.title: 🏆 Engagement — points, badges and weekly awards

panels.description: Share of the findings posted in range that got at least one rating. The team number worth moving: bounded at 100%, so it cannot be flattered by one enthusiastic rater.

targets.rawSql:
-- Share of the findings posted in range that carry at least one human rating.
-- COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) rather than COUNT(*): comment_scores is unique on
-- (note_id, user_id, emoji), so a rater who clicked 3 then 4 without revoking
-- the 3 has two rows and would otherwise be counted twice.
SELECT
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT rc.note_id), 0),
    1
  ) AS "Coverage"
FROM review_comments rc
LEFT JOIN comment_scores cs ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(rc.received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND rc.project_path IN ($project);

panels.title: Rating coverage (target 80%)

panels.description: One winner per ISO week, project and category, settled by the collector and announced in Mattermost. Five categories rather than one leaderboard, so more than one person can top something.

targets.rawSql:
-- Winners per ISO week, as settled by the collector (collector/engagement.py).
-- Stored rather than recomputed here: a closed week's result is a fact, and the
-- Mattermost announcement and this panel have to still agree a year from now.
SELECT
  week_start :: timestamptz AS "Week of",
  iso_week AS "Week",
  CASE category
    WHEN 'top_rater' THEN '🏅 Top Rater'
    WHEN 'most_points' THEN '🔥 Most Points'
    WHEN 'best_feedback' THEN '💬 Best Feedback'
    WHEN 'fastest' THEN '⚡ Fastest Draw'
    WHEN 'completionist' THEN '🎯 Completionist'
    ELSE category
  END AS "Award",
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Winner",
  CASE category
    WHEN 'fastest' THEN
      CASE WHEN value < 1 THEN ROUND(value * 60) || ' min'
           ELSE ROUND(value :: numeric, 1) || ' h' END
    WHEN 'completionist' THEN ROUND(value) || '%'
    WHEN 'most_points' THEN ROUND(value) || ' pts'
    ELSE ROUND(value) :: text
  END AS "Result"
FROM weekly_awards
WHERE $__timeFilter(week_start :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
ORDER BY week_start DESC, category;

panels.title: Weekly award winners

panels.description: rate a finding 2 · rate a summary 1 · +1 on someone else's MR · +1 within 24h · first substantive reply in a thread 5 · other replies 1. Never scored on the rating value given.

targets.rawSql:
-- Points and level per person. The ledger CTE below is generated from
-- collector/engagement.py::POINTS_LEDGER_SQL — that module is the source of
-- truth for the weights, and this copy must be regenerated if they change.
--
--   rate a finding 2 · rate a summary 1 · +1 someone else's MR · +1 within 24h
--   first substantive reply in a thread 5 · any other reply 1
--
-- Nothing here reads the score the rater gave: paying people for the number they
-- pick would inflate the one signal the ratings exist to measure.
WITH ledger AS (
WITH unified AS (
    SELECT 'finding'::text AS kind, note_id, project_path, mr_id,
           user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
    FROM comment_scores
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'summary'::text AS kind, note_id, project_path, mr_id,
           user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
    FROM summary_scores
),
canonical AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (note_id, user_id)
           kind, note_id, project_path, mr_id,
           user_id, username, user_name, emoji, score, received_at
    FROM unified
    -- latest click wins; emoji breaks a tie so the row is deterministic when two
    -- awards share a received_at (a webhook redelivery burst).
    ORDER BY note_id, user_id, received_at DESC, emoji DESC
),
scores AS (
    SELECT c.kind,
           c.note_id,
           c.project_path,
           c.mr_id,
           c.username,
           c.user_name,
           -- Present for *quality* reads only (the agent's own grade). No
           -- engagement weight anywhere in this module reads it: paying a rater
           -- for the number they picked would inflate the one signal the ratings
           -- exist to measure.
           c.score,
           c.received_at AS rated_at,
           COALESCE(rc.mr_author_username, rs.mr_author_username) AS mr_author_username,
           COALESCE(rc.received_at, rs.received_at)               AS artifact_posted_at
    FROM canonical c
    LEFT JOIN review_comments  rc ON c.kind = 'finding' AND rc.note_id = c.note_id
    LEFT JOIN review_summaries rs ON c.kind = 'summary' AND rs.note_id = c.note_id
)

SELECT project_path,
       username,
       user_name,
       to_char((rated_at::timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00' AS occurred_at,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 'rate_finding' ELSE 'rate_summary' END AS action,
       kind,
       mr_id,
       note_id,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END AS base_points,
       CASE WHEN mr_author_username IS NOT NULL AND mr_author_username <> username THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS peer_bonus,
       CASE WHEN artifact_posted_at IS NOT NULL AND rated_at::timestamptz <= artifact_posted_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS speed_bonus,
       (CASE WHEN kind = 'finding' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END)
       + (CASE WHEN mr_author_username IS NOT NULL AND mr_author_username <> username THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
       + (CASE WHEN artifact_posted_at IS NOT NULL AND rated_at::timestamptz <= artifact_posted_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS points
FROM scores
WHERE username IS NOT NULL

UNION ALL

SELECT project_path,
       username,
       user_name,
       occurred_at,
       'reply' AS action,
       kind,
       mr_id,
       note_id,
       points AS base_points,
       0 AS peer_bonus,
       0 AS speed_bonus,
       points
FROM (
    SELECT cr.project_path,
           cr.author_username AS username,
           cr.author_name     AS user_name,
           to_char((cr.received_at::timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00' AS occurred_at,
           COALESCE(cr.parent_kind, 'finding') AS kind,
           cr.mr_id,
           cr.note_id,
           -- Full value for the first substantive reply in a thread; a token
           -- acknowledgement, or a follow-up in a thread this person has already
           -- replied to, earns 1. The weight goes to the reply that carries the
           -- feedback rather than to the count of replies.
           CASE WHEN length(btrim(COALESCE(cr.body, ''))) >= 15
                     AND row_number() OVER (
                         PARTITION BY cr.author_username, cr.discussion_id
                         ORDER BY cr.received_at
                     ) = 1
                THEN 5 ELSE 1 END AS points
    FROM comment_replies cr
    WHERE cr.author_username IS NOT NULL
) replies
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Who",
  SUM(points) :: int AS "Points",
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(points) >= 400 THEN '💎 Diamond'
    WHEN SUM(points) >= 150 THEN '🥇 Gold'
    WHEN SUM(points) >= 50 THEN '🥈 Silver'
    ELSE '🥉 Bronze'
  END AS "Level",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE action <> 'reply') :: int AS "Ratings",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'reply') :: int AS "Replies",
  SUM(peer_bonus) :: int AS "Peer",
  SUM(speed_bonus) :: int AS "Speed"
FROM ledger
WHERE $__timeFilter(occurred_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY username, user_name
ORDER BY "Points" DESC;

panels.title: Points & levels

panels.description: Durable badges. Dated to when the threshold was crossed, not when the row was written, so backfilled history reads truthfully.

targets.rawSql:
-- Every badge each person holds. Achievements are a ratchet: awarded_at is when
-- the threshold was *crossed* (derived from the rating or reply that crossed it),
-- so this is truthful for weeks credited by the 0011 backfill too.
SELECT
  COALESCE(user_name, '@' || username) AS "Who",
  COUNT(*) AS "Badges",
  STRING_AGG(CASE achievement_key
    WHEN 'first_rating' THEN '🌱'
    WHEN 'ratings_10' THEN '⭐'
    WHEN 'ratings_50' THEN '🌟'
    WHEN 'ratings_100' THEN '💯'
    WHEN 'ratings_500' THEN '🏛️'
    WHEN 'first_reply' THEN '💬'
    WHEN 'replies_10' THEN '📝'
    WHEN 'replies_50' THEN '🗣️'
    WHEN 'peer_10' THEN '🤝'
    WHEN 'peer_50' THEN '🧭'
    WHEN 'fast_10' THEN '⚡'
    WHEN 'fast_50' THEN '🚀'
    WHEN 'streak_4w' THEN '🔥'
    WHEN 'streak_12w' THEN '🧗'
    WHEN 'streak_26w' THEN '🏔️'
    WHEN 'perfect_1' THEN '🎯'
    WHEN 'perfect_5' THEN '🏆'
    WHEN 'perfect_20' THEN '👑'
    ELSE '🏅'
  END, ' ' ORDER BY awarded_at) AS "Unlocked"
FROM achievements
WHERE $__timeFilter(awarded_at :: timestamptz)
  AND project_path IN ($project)
GROUP BY username, user_name
ORDER BY "Badges" DESC;

panels.title: Achievement wall

panels.description: Of the findings left on your merge requests, how many got rated. The fairest metric here — it cannot be farmed by volume.

targets.rawSql:
-- Coverage per developer: of the findings the reviewer left on their merge
-- requests, how many carry a rating (by anyone). Bounded at 100%, so unlike a
-- rating count it cannot be farmed by volume — which is why it is the fair
-- metric to hold people to.
SELECT
  rc.mr_author_username AS "Developer",
  COUNT(DISTINCT rc.note_id) AS "Findings received",
  COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) AS "Rated",
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT cs.note_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT rc.note_id)
  ) AS "Coverage %"
FROM review_comments rc
LEFT JOIN comment_scores cs ON cs.note_id = rc.note_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(rc.received_at :: timestamptz)
  AND rc.project_path IN ($project)
  AND rc.mr_author_username IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY rc.mr_author_username
ORDER BY "Coverage %" DESC;
